answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 6 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The mirror multiplier is published, charged in beacon, and atlas lists each payment. A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2156 identities would post 1446 proofs and burn roughly 89 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
